Series::logcumsumexp¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::logcumsumexp() const -> Series
Series::logcumsumexp(std::int64_t dim) const -> Series

What It Does¶

logcumsumexp() is the running (prefix) version of logsumexp(). Along the chosen axis, position t holds

logcumsumexp(x)[t] = log( sum_{j <= t} exp(x[j]) )

So it does not reduce the axis away — it keeps the full length and replaces each position with the log-sum-exp of everything up to and including that position. For a row [1, 2, 3] the result is [1, log(e^1 + e^2), log(e^1 + e^2 + e^3)].

It is the log-space analogue of cumsum(): the same prefix-scan shape, but adding probabilities that are carried as log-scores. It shows up in the forward pass of sequence models — CTC, the forward algorithm for HMMs, autoregressive normalizers — anywhere a running total of exponentials would otherwise overflow.

Like logsumexp(), it is evaluated with a max-shift so exp() cannot overflow:

M = max(x)                       (along the scanned axis)
logcumsumexp(x) = M + log(cumsum(exp(x - M)))

The default axis is the last one.

Parameters¶

dim (std::int64_t, optional)

The axis to scan. Negative values count from the back. Omitted: the last axis.

Returns¶

Series The same shape as the input, each position replaced by the prefix log-sum-exp along dim. Floating point.

Gradient¶

logcumsumexp() is differentiable. Its backward is a cumulative softmax: the sensitivity of output t is spread over inputs 0..t in proportion to exp(x[j]), so an early input feeds many outputs and a late input feeds few.

Examples¶

Example 1. A prefix scan along a length-3 row.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}).logcumsumexp(0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.0000, 2.3133, 3.4076]

The first entry is just x[0], and the last matches logsumexp([1, 2, 3]) = 3.4076.

Example 2. The max-shift keeps it stable where the naive x.exp().cumsum(dim).log() would overflow. Every element is 1000.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({1000.0, 1000.0, 1000.0}).logcumsumexp(0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1000.0000, 1000.6931, 1001.0986]

The differences are log(1), log(2), log(3).

Example 3. -inf prefixes stay -inf (a zero-probability prefix) without NaN.

double ninf = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({ninf, ninf, 2.0}).logcumsumexp(0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-inf, -inf, 2.0000]

Example 4. Scanning one axis of a matrix.

auto m = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, 2.0, 3.0},
    {3.0, 2.0, 1.0},
});

std::cout << m.logcumsumexp(1);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2.3132617, 3.407606],
  [3, 3.3132617, 3.407606]]

Each row is scanned independently.

Example 5. The backward pass is a cumulative softmax.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.logcumsumexp(0).sum().reverse();

std::cout << "dx=" << x.sensitivity();

Output¶

dx=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.358972, 0.97578705, 0.66524096]

Position 0 contributes to all three prefix sums, so it accumulates the most; position 2 contributes only to the last, so it accumulates softmax([1, 2, 3])[2] = 0.665.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • logcumsumexp() is a scan, not a reduction: the output keeps the full axis length.

  • Use it rather than x.exp().cumsum(dim).log(), which overflows for large values.

  • An all--inf prefix stays -inf; a NaN propagates forward through the scan.

  • Floating-point input.

Summary¶

logcumsumexp(x) is the prefix log(sum(exp(...))) along an axis:

  • shape-preserving scan, default axis is the last

  • max-shifted so exp() cannot overflow

  • differentiable, backward is a cumulative softmax
